sections.title: 5 2 CPK C |  U nited States Air B rake and Train H andling
sections.text:
5 2 CPK C |  U nited States Air B rake and Train H andling
5.0  Leaving E q u ip m ent Unattended
5.1  G eneral  R eq u irem ents
W hen leaving railway equipment unattended, the following will apply:
• A single piece of equipment must be left with the hand brake applied.
• A single piece of equipment with a defective hand brake must be left coupled to equipment with 
an operative hand brake.
• Two or more pieces of equipment must be left with a sufficient number of hand brakes.
• W hen hand brakes are not adequate, block the wheels .
• W hen it is required to remove equipment from a previously secured track or train, ensure the 
equipment left standing is properly secured with hand brakes.
• D o not uncouple from or allow equipment to move under its own momentum into standing 
equipment unless it is known that the number of hand brakes applied on the standing equipment 
are sufficient to prevent movement of all equipment.
5.2  Leaving Lo c o m o tive( s )  Unattended
To secure unattended locomotive(s), perform the following:
• Apply hand brakes to each locomotive.
• Test hand brake effectiveness.
• Condition one control stand as a lead locomotive.
o Independent brake cut in and fully applied.
o Automatic brake cut in and 20-psi reduction.
o Generator Field Off.
o Engine Run and Control / Fuel Pump On.
o Engine Control Switch to Isolate.
o Reverser handle removed.
• Turn off all unnecessary lights and close all windows.
• Lock all doors on each locomotive, unless being left in one of the following yards or terminals with 
24  hour per day oversight :
o Artesia, B eaumont, B ensenville, H eavener, J ackson, K ansas City, K endleton, Laredo, M ason 
City, M eridian, M onroe, M ossville, N ahant, Pittsburg, Saratoga Springs, Shreveport, St. 
Louis, St. Paul, or W ylie .
5.3  Leaving a P o rtio n o f  a Train o r C ars  Unattended
To secure a portion of a train or cars being left unattended, perform the following:
• Apply a sufficient number of hand brakes.
• Test hand brake effectiveness.
• M ake an automatic brake reduction sufficient to prevent movement .
• The locomotive engineer must advise the crewmember when the angle cock can be closed.
• Cut away from the equipment and ensure an emergency brake application occurs.
• Leave the angle cock fully open.
o The angle cock may be closed for the purpose of immediately running around equipment to 
open an angle cock or couple to the other end.
CPKC | United States Air Brake and Train Handling 53
• Crew members are responsible to verbally confirm that equipment is being left in accordance with 
these instructions.
5.4 Leaving a Train Unattended
To secure an unattended train, perform the following:
• Apply a sufficient number of hand brakes to the car(s) in the train.
• Test hand brake effectiveness.
• Apply hand brakes to each locomotive in the lead consist.
• Leave the lead locomotive of the unattended train conditioned as follows:
o Independent brake cut in and fully applied.
o Automatic brake cut in and 20-psi reduction.
o Generator Field Off.
o Engine Run and Control / Fuel Pump On.
o Engine Control Switch to Isolate.
o Reverser handle removed.
• Turn off all unnecessary lights and close all windows.
• Lock all doors on each locomotive, including remotes.

54 CPK C |  United States Air Brake and Train Handling
56 C P K C  |  United States A ir Brake and Train H andling
sections.text:
56 C P K C  |  United States A ir Brake and Train H andling
1.0 G eneral Instru c tions
1.1 L oc om otiv e E ngineer Responsib ilities
Locomotive engineers must be familiar with current information regarding locomotive systems and 
mechanical procedures and are responsible for the equipment in their care. 
Locomotive engineers must employ proper train handling techniques to:
• P revent damage to track structure, equipment, and lading.
• Utiliz e the most fuel-efficient means of operation consistent with good train handling.
• Ensure safe, efficient, and productive operation.
P roper train handling will depend on various factors. Locomotive engineers must consider the following 
while pre-trip planning and operating a train:
• Train marshalling.
• Train tonnage and length.
• Tons per operative brake.
• Speed.
• G rade.
• Temperature and weather conditions.
• A mount of slack in train.
• Throttle response characteristics of locomotive consist(s).
• A vailable throttle and dynamic braking effort .
• Dynamic brake type and limitations.
• N umber and placement of cushioned drawbars in the train.
• Block signal spacing.
1.2 Cou pling P ortions of a Train
When coupling together two portions of a train, a brake pipe reduction of 3 5-psi must be 
made before opening the angle cock, unless train movement can be prevented with the 
locomotive brakes.
1.3  In- Train F orc es
C ontrolling and limiting in- train forces are essential for safe train operation. Unless an emergency or other 
condition requires immediate speed reduction, change throttle and dynamic brake positions slowly and 
utiliz e split reductions with the automatic brake to allow train slack adequate time to adjust. 
1.4 Train Separation and Stall Req u irem ents
1.4.1 G eneral Req u irem ents
Train stalls and separations must be reported to the train dispatcher and territory Road F oreman. Where 
possible, broken knuckles must be captured or placed in a location where they can be retrieved by 
management. Locomotive engineers are required to complete and submit required train stall and 
separation report form(s). 
CPKC | United States Air Brake and Train Handling 57
1.4.2 Responding to a Train Stall
Upon stall, the locomotive engineer must:
• Maintain throttle in position 5 or higher.
• Make a 15-psi automatic brake reduction.
• Monitor gauges and surroundings to ensure the train does not roll backwards.
• Once confirmed that the train is stationary and the automatic brake reduction is sufficient to hold 
the train, the throttle can be slowly reduced to Idle.
• If the train begins to move backwards:
o Increase the throttle. 
o Increase the automatic brake reduction.
• If movement continues: 
o Rapidly move throttle to Idle, reverser to reverse, move handle to DB 8, place the train in 
emergency.
o Secure the train in accordance with securement rules.
1.5 Winter Conditions
When snow or ice buildup is present, operate locomotive(s) through yard and industry tracks, or crossings 
within these tracks, prior to moving equipment. Exercise extreme caution when making movements 
through crossings with minimal rail activity or high levels of vehicular traffic.
2.0 Use of Independent Brake
The following requirements apply while using the independent brake:
• The independent brake valve on the controlling locomotive must remain cut in at all times and the 
handle must not be blocked in the actuate position.
• When it is desired to prevent the locomotive brakes from applying during an automatic brake 
application, the independent brake valve handle must be actuated prior to the automatic brake 
application and held until exhaust ceases, but no less than four seconds per locomotive.
• Except when starting or stopping a train or operating with light locomotive(s), the independent 
brake must not be applied while in power or dynamic brake.
• The independent brake may be used in conjunction with dynamic braking, only at speeds of 10 
mph and lower.
• Light independent brake, not to exceed 15-psi, may be used to control wheel slip at speeds below 
10 mph.
• When conditions require the independent brakes to be applied, brake cylinder pressure must be 
controlled to prevent overheating or sliding of the locomotive wheels, excessive slack action, and 
high in-train forces. 
• The independent brake must be fully applied when locomotive(s) are stationary.
C P K C  |  U n i t e d  S t a t e s A i r  B r a ke  a n d  T r a i n  H a n d l i n g56

• When it is desired to prevent the locomotive brakes from applying during an automatic brake 
application, the independent brake valve handle must be actuated prior to the automatic brake 
application and held until exhaust ceases, but no less than four seconds per locomotive.
• Except when starting or stopping a train or operating with light locomotive(s), the independent 
brake must not be applied while in power or dynamic brake.
• The independent brake may be used in conjunction with dynamic braking, only at speeds of 10 
mph and lower.
• Light independent brake, not to exceed 15-psi, may be used to control wheel slip at speeds below 
10 mph.
• When conditions require the independent brakes to be applied, brake cylinder pressure must be 
controlled to prevent overheating or sliding of the locomotive wheels, excessive slack action, and 
high in-train forces. 
• The independent brake must be fully applied when locomotive(s) are stationary.

sections.title: 58 CPK C |  U nited States Air Brake and Train Handling
sections.text:
58 CPK C |  U nited States Air Brake and Train Handling
3.0 U se of  the Automatic Brake
3.1 G eneral Req uirements
The following general requirements apply to the use of air brakes:
• U se of the regulating valve to make brake pipe reductions is prohibited.
• If brake pipe pressure is reduced below 4 8 -psi while making service brake applications, the train 
must be stopped and recharged.
• A train must not be started until the air brakes are fully released.
o In the absences of brake pipe flow indication or rear car pressure reading, allow one minute 
for every 25 cars in the train.
• W hen possible, wait at least 30 seconds between split reductions.
• U se the automatic brake to control a light locomotive consist of seven or more locomotives. D o 
not bail the locomotive brakes unless a release is required.
3.2 Apply ing or Reapply ing the Automatic Brake
W hen applying or reapplying the brakes, use the equaliz ing reservoir to measure reductions 
as follows:
C onv entional Trains
• W hen the train air brake system is fully charged, make at least a 7 -psi reduction.
• W hen the train air brake system is not fully charged, use one of the following methods to apply 
the automatic brake:
o D etermine the amount of false gradient in the train and reduce the equaliz ing reservoir 
pressure 7 -psi plus the amount of false gradient (True Gradient – False Gradient +  7 -psi).
o Make an automatic brake reduction at least 7 -psi below the rear car brake pipe pressure.
o Make at least a 7 -psi reduction below the point where brake pipe pressure begins to ex haust .
o W hen a train equipped with an EOT does not display rear car pressure, make an automatic 
brake reduction of at least 5-psi more than the last reduction.
D istrib uted P ow er Trains
• W hen the train air brake system is fully charged, make at least a 7 -psi reduction.
• W hen the train air brake system is not fully charged, use one of the following methods to apply 
the automatic brake:
o W hen the train has only one remote consist which is located on the rear of the train, make at 
least a 7 -psi reduction below the point where brake pipe pressure begins to ex haust .
o W hen the rear car pressure is known, determine the amount of false gradient in the train and 
reduce the equaliz ing reservoir 7 -psi plus the amount of false gradient.
o W hen the train has multiple remotes with at least one remote consist located on the rear of 
the train, or a train equipped with an EOT that does not display rear car pressure, make an 
automatic brake reduction of at least 5-psi more than the last reduction.
CPKC | United States Air Brake and Train Handling 59
• If the automatic brake valve is moved to the full service position and an additional automatic 
brake reduction is required to control train speed, the train must be immediately stopped and 
recharged. Hand brakes may be required to secure the train while the brake system is recharged.
3.3 Releasing the Automatic Brake
At slow speeds, evaluate the following conditions before attempting a running release of the automatic 
brakes:
• Train speed.
• Train makeup.
• Physical characteristics of the territory.
• Location of remote consist(s) and recharge characteristics.
• Train length.
• Brake pipe leakage.
Following a release of the automatic brake on trains equipped with an EOT, the throttle must not be 
increased, or dynamic brake reduced until the EOT pressure increases at least 3-psi and sufficient time 
has been allowed for the brakes to release.
On trains configured with a remote locomotive positioned at the rear of the train, the throttle 
must not be increased or dynamic brake reduced until the locomotive air flow indicates the brakes are 
released.
A running release may not be appropriate in all situations. Trains may be required to stop to comply with 
these instructions.
4.0 Train Braking Issues
4.1 Reporting Train Braking Issues
Immediately report the following to the train dispatcher:
• Any occurrence of an undesired release of the brakes.
• An automatic brake reduction of 20-psi or greater while moving.
• Abnormal flow or brake pipe gradient.
• A train that is not braking as anticipated.
Report must include the train’s specific location, nature of the issue, current weather conditions, and any 
other relevant information.
4.2 Responding to Train Braking Issues
If an undesired release occurs while the automatic brake is applied, increase the automatic brake pipe 
reduction by at least 5-psi. The train may be placed in emergency, if necessary. 
If unintended movement occurs while the train is stopped with air brakes set, increase the automatic 
brake pipe reduction by at least 5-psi. The train may be placed in emergency, if necessary. Once 
stopped, the train must be immediately secured with hand brakes.
Application of handbrakes will be governed by Securing Equipment Following an Emergency Brake 
Application or Train Braking Issue on Heavy or Mountain Grade in the Securement Chapter.

sections.title: 60 CPK C |  United States Air Brake and Train Handling
sections.text:
60 CPK C |  United States Air Brake and Train Handling
5 .0 Delayed Departu re in N on - Signal Territory
Anytime a train is stopped in non- signal territory, comply with the following:
C onv entional Trains
• Make at least a 10- psi reduction with the automatic brake.
• When ready to depart, release the automatic brake.
• If brake pipe pressure is being restored, the train may proceed.
• If brake pipe pressure is not being restored, the train may operate up to one train length at a 
speed not to exceed 10 mph.
o If the brake pipe pressure fails to restore during this time, the train must be stopped and 
inspected.
o The train may depart when continuity is restored.
Distrib u ted P ow er Trains
Complete a Train Check complying with related procedures.
E x ceptions
The procedures listed above do not apply to conventional or distributed power trains when:
• A brief stop is made to line switches or comply with signal indications.
• O n grades where train handling techniq ues req uire air brake to remain applied when initiating 
movement.
6 .0 M inimiz ing Sticking Brakes
Sticking brakes occur when car air brakes remain applied after the automatic brake is released. When a 
sticking brake is identified:
• Stop the train as soon as possible, consistent with good train handling.
• Make a 2 0- psi reduction and allow sufficient time for air pressure to stabilize.
• If necessary, cut out the control valve or set out the car.
Utilize the following methods to minimize sticking brakes:
• Do not overcharge the air brake system.
• When the automatic brake is used to stop a train, make a reduction no less than 10- psi.
• When coupling cars to the rear end of a train, before opening the angle cock make a minimum 
reduction of at least 10- psi.
• When a running release of the automatic brake is to be made, if operating conditions permit, 
increase the automatic brake pipe reduction to at least 10- psi and allow the air brakes to stabilize 
before releasing.
CPKC | United States Air Brake and Train Handling 61
7.0 Use of Throttle
7.1 Throttle Handling
When it is desired to increase speed, the throttle must be advanced one notch at a time. Tractive effort or 
amperage must be constant or dropping before moving the throttle to the next higher position. When it is 
desired to decrease speed, the throttle must be reduced gradually, except in emergency situations. The 
throttle must always be handled in a manner that results in smooth operation.
In addition:
• Do not change the generator field switch position while in throttle.
• Unless authorized to do so, do not utilize the throttle to hold a train stationary on a grade.
• After releasing the dynamic brake in preparation for applying power, the throttle must be 
advanced with care to ensure gradual adjustment of train slack.
7.2 Short Time Ratings
Short time rating limits apply to DC type locomotives when operating at high amperage levels. Do not 
exceed the short time ratings listed on the load meter or rating plate. Do not operate the locomotive 
continuously for more than the maximum time listed without stopping to cool the traction motors. Short 
time ratings are not cumulative. 
When short time rating limitations exist and amperage levels are not displayed on the lead locomotive, 
the following will apply:
Speed
• 11 MPH – Continuous.
• 10.5 MPH – 60 Minutes.
• 10 MPH – 30 Minutes.
• 9 MPH – 15 minutes.
• 8 MPH – 10 minutes.
• 5 MPH – 5 minutes.
8.0 Use of Dynamic Brake
8.1 Dynamic Brake Factor
A dynamic brake factor is a numerical value used to convey the dynamic braking capability of a 
locomotive. The following dynamic brake factors will apply based on locomotive type:
Dynamic Brake Factors
• Dynamic Brake Factor 4:
o All 4 axle locomotives (except GP60).
• Dynamic Brake Factor 6:
o GP60.
o SD30.
o SD40.
o SD50.

When the Dynamic B rake factor of a foreign locomotive is unknown, the following will apply:

8.2 Dynamic Brake Limitations
Dynamic brake limits refer to the effort value, K lbs or amps, displayed on the lead locomotive gauge or 
screen. Do not exceed a dynamic brake factor of 2 0 on any locomotive consist. If the dynamic brake must 
be cut out on a locomotive without a cut out switch, the locomotive must be isolated.
The following will apply when the dynamic brake factor of the lead locomotive consist is 
10 or greater:
• When operating on other than main track, or any track with a maximum speed of 15 mph or less, 
the DB  effort must not exceed 6 0 K lbs ( AC )  or 500 amps ( DC ) .
• When operating through any turnout, the DB  effort must not exceed 6 0 K lbs or 
500 amps ( DC ) :
o C onventional trains : Prior to the turnout, and until at least half the movement has passed the 
turnout.
o Distributed Power trains: prior to the turnout, and until the entire movement has passed the 
turnout. 
• When governed by a temporary speed restriction, the DB  effort must not exceed 4 0 K lbs ( AC )  or 
3 50 amps ( DC ) :
o C onventional trains : one-half mile prior to the restriction, and until the locomotive( s)  are clear 
of the restriction.
o Distributed Power trains: one-half mile prior to the restriction, and until the entire movement is 
clear of the restriction.
o Exception: when any portion of such restriction is on a Heavy or Mountain grade, the DB  
effort must not exceed 6 0 K lbs ( AC )  or 500 amps ( DC ) .
• When governed by a Heat S low restriction, the DB  effort must not exceed 6 0 K lbs ( AC )  or 500 
amps ( DC )  until the entire movement is clear of the restriction. 
CPKC | United States Air Brake and Train Handling 63
8.3 Dynamic Brake Operation
The following requirements will apply to use of dynamic brakes:
• Pause in Idle for 10 seconds when transitioning from throttle to dynamic brake.
• If the wheel slip light illuminates while using the dynamic brake:
o Reduce the dynamic brake handle position until the light goes out.
o If the light continues to illuminate, stop the train and inspect the locomotives to ensure the 
wheels are rotating freely.
• When transitioning into dynamic braking, move the handle slowly to gradually bunch slack and 
minimize in-train forces.
9.0 Emergency Brake and Penalty Brake Applications
9.1 Location of Emergency Brake Valves
Employees must be familiar with the location and operation of emergency brake valves on locomotives 
and cars, if equipped. 
9.2 Emergency Brake Application by Crew Member
A crew member must initiate an emergency brake application, when:
• Threat to life, personal injury, or property damage is imminent.
• The locomotive engineer becomes incapacitated or does not respond to warnings or signals to 
reduce train speed or stop the train.
• There is doubt or uncertainty that service brake applications can control train speed.
9.3 Exceeding Maximum Authorized Speed
When a train is descending a section of track defined as heavy or mountain grade and the train exceeds 
the maximum authorized speed by 5 mph or more, the train shall be immediately brought to a stop using 
an emergency brake application, if necessary.
9.4 Emergency Application and Undesired Emergency Procedures
To make an emergency brake application or respond to an undesired emergency application:
• Move the automatic brake valve handle to the emergency position.
• Activate the emergency toggle switch on the HOT if train is equipped with an EOT.
• While actuating, move the independent brake handle to a position that will develop the desired 
amount of brake cylinder pressure without sliding the wheels or developing excessive in-train 
forces.
o Do not actuate when operating light locomotive consists.
• When the desired locomotive brake cylinder pressure is achieved, stop actuating the independent 
brake.
• To the extent possible, maintain the current slack condition to avoid the development of 
excessive in-train forces.
• If the emergency application occurs while in throttle, monitor gauges to ensure tractive effort 
reduces to zero. If tractive effort remains, move the throttle handle to idle.

sections.title: 64 CPKC |  U nited States Air B rake and Train H andling
sections.text:
64 CPKC |  U nited States Air B rake and Train H andling
9 .5  P enalty  B rake Application
When a penalty brake application occurs:
• If necessary, control the amount of independent brake cylinder pressure by moving the 
independent brake handle to the application z one while actuating.
• Move the automatic brake handle to the suppression position.
• R eturn throttle to Idle or dynamic brake to the off position.
• If operating conditions permit, after stopping and when the PCS closes, move the automatic 
brake handle to the release position.
9 .6  Emergency  Reversal of Locomotive Traction Motors
In emergency situations only, when all other means of stopping a train are exhausted, locomotive traction 
motors can be reversed. This procedure may be haz ardous to personnel and equipment and should only 
be used as a last resort. If necessary to reverse the traction motors, comply with the following:
• Alert all employees on the locomotive.
• Place the throttle in Idle.
• Place the reverser handle in the position opposite the direction of travel.
• Advance the throttle to notch 1.
10.0 Shoving Movements
10.1 G eneral Req uirements
U se extreme care and good j udgement while making shove movements. When beginning a shoving 
movement, use the lowest amount of tractive effort necessary to cause the equipment to move. To avoid 
j ackknifing, wheel climb, or rail turnover, these factors must be considered before making a shoving 
movement:
• Long car/short car combinations and location in train.
• The number of empty cars near the head end of the train or remote consist( s) .
• The amount of tractive effort produced.
• The number of locomotives that do not have alignment control couplers.
• Track curvature and grade.
CPKC | United States Air Brake and Train Handling 65
10.2 Limitations While Shoving
The following limitations apply while making shoving movements and will be measured using the tractive 
effort or amperage value displayed on the controlling locomotive:
Maximum Allowable Tractive Effort
AC Locomotives
Locomotive Count Operating Through Curves

While switching cars, comply with the following:
• Gradually stretch or bunch slack when starting or stopping switching movements.
• Control buff and draft forces.
12.0 Operating Through Water
12.1 Response to Water Above the Top of Rail
Locomotives must not be operated, in throttle or idle, through water greater than 6 inches above the top 
of rail. This does not apply to rail cars provided movements are made in a push/pull fashion and 
locomotives are not moved through the water.
The following guidelines will govern response to water above the top of rail:
• A movement unexpectedly encountering water at any height above the top of rail must:
o Make every effort to stop.
o Immediately notify the train dispatcher.
o Not proceed until the train dispatcher has confirmed with Engineering services that the water 
is 6 inches or less above the top of rail and the track structure is safe for movements.
• Should a movement unexpectedly operate through water at any height above the top 
of rail:
o The movement must be stopped with the locomotives clear of the water.
o The crew must immediately advise the train dispatcher and Mechanical department.

9 .5  P enalty  B rake Application
When a penalty brake application occurs:
• If necessary, control the amount of independent brake cylinder pressure by moving the 
independent brake handle to the application z one while actuating.
• Move the automatic brake handle to the suppression position.
• R eturn throttle to Idle or dynamic brake to the off position.
• If operating conditions permit, after stopping and when the PCS closes, move the automatic 
brake handle to the release position.
9 .6  Emergency  Reversal of Locomotive Traction Motors
In emergency situations only, when all other means of stopping a train are exhausted, locomotive traction 
motors can be reversed. This procedure may be haz ardous to personnel and equipment and should only 
be used as a last resort. If necessary to reverse the traction motors, comply with the following:
• Alert all employees on the locomotive.
• Place the throttle in Idle.
• Place the reverser handle in the position opposite the direction of travel.
• Advance the throttle to notch 1.

• The amount of tractive effort produced.
• The number of locomotives that do not have alignment control couplers.
• Track curvature and grade.

sections.text:
66 CPK C |  U nited States Air Brake and Train Handling
o The locomotive engineer must operate the traction motor blowers for 10 minutes per traction 
motor blower procedures.
o The movement must not proceed until the train dispatcher has confirmed with Engineering 
services that the water is 6 inches or less above the top of rail.
12 .2  Traction Motor B l ow er Procedu res
The following procedures will govern operation of traction motor blowers in response to water above the 
top of the rail.
EMD  Locomotives w ith  D C Traction Motors
• Ensure the locomotive is stopped with the reverser centered.
• Place the generator field switch to Off.
• Advance the throttle to notch 8  to increase the volume of air traveling through the 
traction motors.
• Confirm air is blowing from the traction motor vents.
SD 7 0ACU , SD 7 0ACE, SD 7 0MACe Locomotives
• Ensure the locomotive is stopped with the reverser centered.
• On the main operator FIRE screen, Select Screen Controls.
• Navigate to the Locomotive Data page.
• Select Self Tests.
• Select the Traction Motor Blower test.
• Ensure all entry conditions for the test are met.
• Select Start and begin the test.
• Check the traction motor blower for abnormal sounds or vibrations.
• Notify Mechanical when abnormal conditions exist.
• Confirm air is blowing from the traction motor vents.
• After a minimum of 10 minutes, exit the test.
AC4400CW and C44- 9 W Locomotives
• Ensure the locomotive is stopped with the throttle in Idle.
• Open the cabinet doors behind the center seat.
• Toggle the Diagnostic Access Switch to gain access to the DID Panel.
• On the DID Panel, select Set, 2 , Do_It .
• Select Test.
• Confirm the following be selecting Did_It.
• Air pressure.
• LCCB breaker is up.
• Disconnect all MU  cables .
• G enerator field braker is up .
• COB breaker is up.
• Engine control switch is in Run.
• PCS is reset.
• Select Manual, New Test, Eq uipment Blower (Test 2 61 or 2 62 ), Do_It .
• Follow any set up instructions displayed on the screen.
CPKC | United States Air Brake and Train Handling 67
• When all set up conditions are met, select Full Speed, then Do_It.
• Check the traction motor blower for abnormal sounds or vibrations.
• Notify Mechanical when abnormal conditions exist.
• Confirm air is blowing from the traction motor vents.
• Perform Half Speed and Quarter Speed Tests.
• Check the traction motor blow for abnormal sounds or vibrations.
• Notify Mechanical when abnormal conditions exist.
• Confirm air is blowing from the traction motor vents.
• After a minimum of 10 minutes, select Off and exit the test.
AC44CWM, ES44, and ET44 Locomotives
• Ensure the locomotive is stopped with the reverser centered.
• Contact Mechanical to obtain the current password to access level 3.
• From the operator’s smart display screen, select Screen Controls, then Password.
• Enter the level 3 password.
• Navigate to the Loco Tests page.
• Select Self Test.
• Navigate to the Auxiliary Alternator page in the left column (Self Test group).
• Select Traction Blower Control (TBC) test in the Right Column or enter test number 406.
• Select Begin Test and wait for the auxiliary alternator to start up.
• Once the auxiliary alternator is running, select Full Speed.
• Check the traction motor blower for abnormal sounds or vibrations.
• Notify Mechanical when abnormal conditions exist.
• Perform Half Speed test.
• Check the traction motor blow for abnormal sounds or vibrations.
• Notify Mechanical when abnormal conditions exist.
• Confirm air is blowing from the traction motor vents.
• While the tests are running, confirm the amperage on the TBC (3 phases) rises evenly when the 
traction motor blower starts up.
• After a minimum of 10 minutes, exit the test.
13.0 Passenger Trains
13.1 Passenger Train Operations
When operating passenger trains, locomotive engineers are governed by the verbal and written 
instructions provided by the manager of the passenger train. These instructions will also apply to 
business trains.

sections.title: 6 8 CPK C |  United States Air Brake and Train Handling
sections.text:
6 8 CPK C |  United States Air Brake and Train Handling
14 .0 Heavy  and  M ou ntain G rad e Operation
14 .1 G eneral Req u irements
The following handling requirements apply when cresting and descending a heavy or mountain grade. 
Heavy and mountain grade segments are identified in the timetable.
14 .2 Hand ling gu id elines
14 .2.1 G eneral Hand ling
• Train crews shall not operate down heavy or mountain grades where, in their judgement, a 
combination of ambient temperatures and heavy snow or ice conditions are sufficient to make the 
operation unsafe.
• Unless it is known that sufficient braking is available, when cresting hills towards heavy or 
mountain grade, maintain a speed at least 5  mph below maximum authorized speed until braking 
is determined to be ample.
• Early in the braking process, achieve a balance between the level of dynamic brake and the level 
of air brake needed to control train speed on descending grade.
• Where possible, limit automatic brake reductions to allow train speed to be controlled with the 
dynamic brake.
• I f the brake pipe pressure at the rear of the train does not reduce in response to a reduction made 
with the automatic brake, stop the train immediately.
• When conditions warrant, use all available braking power including the emergency brake, 
if necessary.
• When stopped by an emergency application from any source:
o The train must be immediately secured in accordance with securement rules.
o The locomotive engineer must contact the proper authority and receive instruction from a 
Road F oreman if there is doubt or uncertainty that the train can be moved safely .
• Before moving from or recovering an emergency brake application on heavy or mountain grade, 
the crew must:
o Consider train location, grade, proximity of lesser grade, weather, rail, or any other condition 
that may affect braking.
o Contact the proper authority for instruction, should doubt or uncertainty arise.
14 .3  Uncontrolled  M ovements
Any movement that reaches a speed of 5  mph above the maximum authorized tracks speed is 
considered an uncontrolled movement. Uncontrolled movements must be stopped immediately, using an 
emergency brake application, if necessary. After stopping an uncontrolled movement, a train may not 
proceed until it is determined that sufficient braking is available to control the movement.
14 .4 D istribu ted  P ow er T rains in E mergency  w ith  C ommu nication Loss
When a distributed power train is standing in emergency on heavy or mountain grade and communication 
has been lost with one or more remote(s), perform the following:
• Secure the train with hand brakes in accordance with securement rules.
• Ensure the automatic brake handle of the lead locomotive is in emergency.
• End distributed power per instructions listed in Modifying or Ending Distributed Power Set Up.
CPKC | United States Air Brake and Train Handling 69
15.0 Helper Operations
15.1 Use of Helper Locomotive(s)
Helper locomotive(s) may be used to assist a train provided there is not a caboose, riding platform, or 
crew transportation car at the rear of the train being assisted. 
15.2 Operating Responsibilities 
Comply with the following during helper operation:
• Exercise caution and good judgement at all times.
• When adding helpers to other locomotives on a train, control of all locomotives coupled together 
must be transferred to the lead locomotive engineer by plugging in the MU cable, whenever 
practicable.
• When more than one locomotive is attached to a train, unless specified in Helper Operation 
instructions, the locomotive engineer in the lead locomotive must control the train’s air brakes.
• Prior to commencing helper operations, a job briefing must be conducted with all crew members 
to ensure understanding of:
o Loads, empties, tonnage, and length.
o Number of operative locomotives.
o Dynamic brake factor.
o Traction motor status.
o Speed.
o Equipment and movement restrictions.
o Braking practices.
o Where helper locomotive(s) will be removed.
• The locomotive engineer located on the leading end of a movement will be in charge of 
the following:
o Movement Communication:
 Limits of authority.
 Signal indications.
 Authorized speed.
 Stopping locations.
 All other information pertinent to the movement.
o Providing warning with locomotive whistle and bell. This includes crossings at grade and 
other situations covered by rule.
• Radio communication between the assisted train and helper locomotive engineer(s) must be 
maintained at all times.
• The throttle of the helper locomotive must be advanced slowly, one notch at a time, maintaining 
the lowest possible effort to begin or maintain movement.
• Do not cut off helper locomotive(s) while the train is moving.
C P K C  |  U n i t e d  S t a t e s A i r  B r a ke  a n d  T r a i n  H a n d l i n g68

sections.text:
7 0 CPK C |  U nited S tates Air B rake and Train H andling
15.3 Placement of Helper Locomotives
15.3.1 G eneral Req u irements
The following will apply to the use of helper locomotive(s):
• The total number of driving ax les at any location in the train may not ex ceed the driving ax le limits 
listed in section 3 .
o E x ception: N o more than 24  driving ax les may be used at the rear of any assisted train.
• A remote consist at the rear of the train must be included in the driving ax le and locomotive count 
in helper operations.
• A TrAM check must be performed to ensure cars immediately ahead of the helper locomotive(s) 
pass R emote Z one rules when:
o Assisting a train with distributed power consist(s) located in-train and no remote consist is 
located at the rear of the train.
o H elper locomotives are placed in -train.
• H elper locomotives must adhere to established limitations for effort and amperage 
while shoving.
• W hile operating with independent control of throttle and brakes, the helper locomotive engineer 
must:
o Follow all train handling commands from the locomotive engineer of the assisted train.
o Immediately reduce the throttle to Idle and apply 5 0 percent of available independent brake if 
there is any indication that an emergency application has occurred while in motion.
o R educe the throttle to Idle, consistent with good train handling, if communication has been 
interrupted with the locomotive engineer of the assisted train and operational requirements 
are uncertain.
15.3.2  Helper Locomotive(s) A ttached to the Head or Rear of a Train
The following requirements will apply to helper locomotives attached to the head or rear of a train.
Brake Pipe Disconnected
For movements that will travel less than three miles, helper locomotive(s) may assist a train with the 
brake pipe disconnected provided a j ob briefing is conducted with the locomotive engineer of the assisted 
train, and it is determined that the movement can be made safely with the brake pipe disconnected. If the 
movement cannot be safely made, follow procedures for brake pipe connected.
The helper locomotive engineer must:
• Obtain permission from the locomotive engineer of the assisted train to couple on.
• If coupling to the head end locomotive or distributed power locomotive:
o W here possible, connect the electrical j umper cable between the helper locomotive(s) and 
the rear distributed power locomotive of the assisted train to allow throttle to be controlled by 
the locomotive engineer of the assisted train.
o Place the automatic brake handle in release.
o R emove the reverser handle.
o Prior to commencing movement, fully release the independent brake.
• If coupling to a railcar:
o Place the automatic brake handle in release.
o Prior to commencing movement, fully release the independent brake.
CPKC | United States Air Brake and Train Handling 71
Brake Pipe Connected
For movements that will travel a distance greater than three miles, control of the train’s air brakes has 
changed, or where brake pipe must be connected, the following procedures will apply:
• The helper locomotive engineer will obtain permission from the locomotive engineer of the 
assisted train to couple on.
• Prior to opening angle cocks, the helper locomotive engineer must:
o Make a 20-psi reduction with the automatic brake.
o Cut out the automatic brake valve and place the handle in the handle off or continuous 
service position.
o Couple the brake pipe hoses.
o Open the angle cock on the helper locomotive.
o Open the angle cock on the car or locomotive of the assisted train.
o Place the independent brake valve handle in the release position and actuate to fully release 
the brakes of the helper locomotive(s).
• Once helper locomotive(s) are added to the train, the locomotive engineer of the assisted train 
must:
o Perform a Class III air brake test.
o Verify with the helper locomotive engineer that brake pipe pressure has reduced and 
increased in accordance with Class III requirements.
15.3.3 Helper Locomotive(s) Detached from the Head or Rear of a Train
After removing helper locomotive(s) from head or rear of an assisted train, perform the following:
• If the brake pipe was connected, the locomotive engineer of the assisted train must perform a 
class III brake test.
• If the brake pipe was not connected, no additional brake test is required.
15.3.4 Helper Locomotive(s) Marshalled into a Train
Perform the following when helper locomotive(s) are marshalled into a train:
• Prior to opening angle cocks, the helper locomotive engineer must:
o Make a 20-psi reduction with the automatic brake.
o Cut out the automatic brake valve and place the handle in the handle off or continuous 
service position.
o Couple the brake pipe hoses.
o Open the angle cocks on each side of the helper locomotive(s) and the assisted train.
o Place the independent brake valve handle in the release position and actuate to fully release 
the brakes of the helper locomotive(s).
• Once helper locomotive(s) are added to the train, the locomotive engineer of the assisted train 
must:
o Perform a Class III brake test.
o Verify with the helper locomotive engineer that brake pipe pressure has reduced and 
increased in accordance with Class III requirements.
15.3.5 Removing Helper Locomotive(s) Marshalled into a Train
After removing helper locomotive(s) from an assisted train, the locomotive engineer of the assisted train 
must perform a Class III air brake test.

15.3.2  Helper Locomotive(s) A ttached to the Head or Rear of a Train
The following requirements will apply to helper locomotives attached to the head or rear of a train.
Brake Pipe Disconnected
For movements that will travel less than three miles, helper locomotive(s) may assist a train with the 
brake pipe disconnected provided a j ob briefing is conducted with the locomotive engineer of the assisted 
train, and it is determined that the movement can be made safely with the brake pipe disconnected. If the 
movement cannot be safely made, follow procedures for brake pipe connected.
The helper locomotive engineer must:
• Obtain permission from the locomotive engineer of the assisted train to couple on.
• If coupling to the head end locomotive or distributed power locomotive:
o W here possible, connect the electrical j umper cable between the helper locomotive(s) and 
the rear distributed power locomotive of the assisted train to allow throttle to be controlled by 
the locomotive engineer of the assisted train.
o Place the automatic brake handle in release.
o R emove the reverser handle.
o Prior to commencing movement, fully release the independent brake.
• If coupling to a railcar:
o Place the automatic brake handle in release.
o Prior to commencing movement, fully release the independent brake.
CPKC | United States Air Brake and Train Handling 71
Brake Pipe Connected
For movements that will travel a distance greater than three miles, control of the train’s air brakes has 
changed, or where brake pipe must be connected, the following procedures will apply:
• The helper locomotive engineer will obtain permission from the locomotive engineer of the 
assisted train to couple on.
• Prior to opening angle cocks, the helper locomotive engineer must:
o Make a 20-psi reduction with the automatic brake.
o Cut out the automatic brake valve and place the handle in the handle off or continuous 
service position.
o Couple the brake pipe hoses.
o Open the angle cock on the helper locomotive.
o Open the angle cock on the car or locomotive of the assisted train.
o Place the independent brake valve handle in the release position and actuate to fully release 
the brakes of the helper locomotive(s).
• Once helper locomotive(s) are added to the train, the locomotive engineer of the assisted train 
must:
o Perform a Class III air brake test.
o Verify with the helper locomotive engineer that brake pipe pressure has reduced and 
increased in accordance with Class III requirements.
15.3.3 Helper Locomotive(s) Detached from the Head or Rear of a Train
After removing helper locomotive(s) from head or rear of an assisted train, perform the following:
• If the brake pipe was connected, the locomotive engineer of the assisted train must perform a 
class III brake test.
• If the brake pipe was not connected, no additional brake test is required.
15.3.4 Helper Locomotive(s) Marshalled into a Train
Perform the following when helper locomotive(s) are marshalled into a train:
• Prior to opening angle cocks, the helper locomotive engineer must:
o Make a 20-psi reduction with the automatic brake.
o Cut out the automatic brake valve and place the handle in the handle off or continuous 
service position.
o Couple the brake pipe hoses.
o Open the angle cocks on each side of the helper locomotive(s) and the assisted train.
o Place the independent brake valve handle in the release position and actuate to fully release 
the brakes of the helper locomotive(s).
• Once helper locomotive(s) are added to the train, the locomotive engineer of the assisted train 
must:
o Perform a Class III brake test.
o Verify with the helper locomotive engineer that brake pipe pressure has reduced and 
increased in accordance with Class III requirements.
15.3.5 Removing Helper Locomotive(s) Marshalled into a Train
After removing helper locomotive(s) from an assisted train, the locomotive engineer of the assisted train 
must perform a Class III air brake test.

CPKC | United States Air Brake and Train Handling 73
1.0 General Requirements
Employees must use the most efficient means available to maximize fuel efficiency. The following will 
apply:
• Locomotive engineers must use the most fuel-efficient methods when operating locomotives, 
consistent with good train handling.
• Dynamic brake is the preferred method of braking.
• Whenever possible, avoid increasing the throttle while the automatic brake is applied.
• Unless authorized by timetable or special instruction, power braking above notch 4 is prohibited.
• When it is known that a train will be delayed, train speed must be reduced to minimize delay time.
• Avoid unnecessary increases in speed over short distances.
2.0 Compliance with Train Document Messages and Other 
Instructions
The locomotive engineer and conductor are jointly responsible to ensure that the number of operating 
locomotives on a train are compliant with train document messages or other related instructions. 
Locomotive engineers must isolate excess locomotive(s) and document locomotive status on the Crew 
Information Form.
3.0 Energy Management Systems
When available, use of energy management software is mandatory. Locomotive engineers who have not 
received training are prohibited from operating energy management software.
Issues with energy management systems must be reported to the applicable support desk and reported 
on the required form.
4.0 Automatic Engine Start Stop (AESS)
4.1 General
Locomotives equipped with automatic engine start/stop systems are identified by labels and instructions 
affixed inside the locomotive cab and at the engine start/stop station. A green Enabled light will be visible 
on the engine control panel, or the control stand on certain automatic start/stop systems to convey 
system status. Warning horns or bells sound before an automatic shut down or restart occurs. Auto 
start/stop equipped locomotives will automatically shut down when conditions permit. The reverser must 
be centered for AESS to work on trailing locomotives.
4.2 Restarting Locomotives Prior to Starting a Movement
Locomotives equipped with automatic engine start and stop systems may have shut down if the 
locomotive(s) have been inactive for an extended duration of time. If it is suspected that any operative 
locomotive(s) has shut down, or if engine run status is unknown, move the reverser handle in the 
direction of travel to activate the engine start sequence. Wait at least two minutes before starting the train.C P K C  |  U n i t e d  S t a t e s A i r  B r a ke  a n d  T r a i n  H a n d l i n g72

sections.text:
74 C P K C  |  U nited S tates A ir B rake and Train H andling
5.0 L ocomotiv e A nti - id ling Req uirements
L ocomotives not eq uipped with A E S S  system must be manually shut down if it is known that the 
locomotive( s)  will be idling for more than 15 minutes, and the ambient temperature is expected 
to remain at or above 40 degrees F ahrenheit. I n the case of uncertainty, contact M echanical. The manual 
shut down req uirement does not apply if the engine must be kept running to:
• M aintain air pressure for the braking system .
• M aintain battery charge on the locomotive for the starting systems.
• H eat or cool the cab or passenger eq uipment for the reasons of health and safety .
• P erform diagnostic testing and necessary maintenance.
• R espond to an emergency situation.
CPKC | United States Air Brake and Train Handling 75
6.0 Pacing 
When it is known that a train will be delayed, the train speed must be reduced to limit delay time and 
amount of fuel consumed. This includes following a slower train, anticipated train meets, and 
maintenance work windows.
The train dispatcher may issue instructions for train speed to be reduced to less than maximum 
authorized timetable speed. To take advantage of areas with descending grade, this restriction only 
applies when the train is operating in throttle. 
When train pacing for an unusually long period of time, take additional locomotives off-line to compensate 
for reduced horsepower needs at lower speeds.

sections.title: 7 6 CPK C |  United States Air Brake and Train H andling
sections.text:
7 6 CPK C |  United States Air Brake and Train H andling
7.0  Trip  O p tim iz er
7.1  G eneral  Req u irem ents
The following req uirements will apply to use of the Trip Optimizer system:
• Crews are responsible to ensure that the information entered into the Trip Optimizer system 
corresponds to the documentation for the train.
• Unless authorized to operate with distributed power locomotive(s) coupled to the lead consist, the 
locomotive engineer must conventionalize all locomotives located on the head end of the train. If 
authorized to proceed, the locomotive engineer must disengage Trip Optimizer or operate in 
manual mode and complete req uired reporting.
7.2 Trip  O p tim iz er – N on - PTC I ntegrated ( S tand- al one)
Non-PTC integrated Trip Optimizer plans a trip based solely on data received during the trip initialization. 
Trip Optimizer will not receive updates or have knowledge of critical operating information such as 
signals, track authority or restrictions that are voided or added during the 
trip. Non-PTC integrated Trip Optimizer is designated for main tracks only. Follow these 
procedures when:
• Initializing a new trip.
• Engaging Auto Control.
• Disengaging Auto Control.
• Using Auto Control Through Main Track Divergence.
7.2.1  I nitial iz e N ew Trip
To initialize a new trip, perform the following:
• Press Trip Optimizer key.
• Press New Trip key.
• Press Yes key.
• Review trip information displayed and if correct, press Accept Trip key.
• Confirm by pressing Yes key.
• If trip information is incorrect, contact the applicable support desk.
7.2.2 Train S etu p  Verification
• Compare locomotive and train information displayed with train documentation received. If correct, 
press the Accept key.
• Confirm by pressing the Yes key.
7.2.3  L ocom otiv e or Train E dits
If Locomotive or Train edits are req uired, changes can be accomplished as follows:
• Change Locomotives – To change the position of any locomotive, highlight that locomotive and 
use the number keys to enter the correct position.
• Remove Locomotive – To remove a locomotive, highlight the locomotive and press the Remove 
Locomotive key.
CPKC | United States Air Brake and Train Handling 77
• Add Locomotive – Enter the initials and number of the added locomotive.
o When locomotives are added, the default power mode is defaulted to isolate. 
The locomotive engineer must assign the correct operating status (Run, Isolate, 
DB Cutout, or DB Only).
o The default position of the added locomotive(s) is 0.
o A new position must be entered using the soft keys on the display screen to save changes to 
the locomotive consist.
On DP trains, it is critical that the position of the remote consist is accurately reflected on the Train Setup 
screen. Location is determined by line number, not loads/empties. Verify positioning and edit if necessary.
7.2.4 Change Power Mode
The Change Power Mode screen indicates the running status of each locomotive for the Trip Optimizer 
system. Power modes are as follows:
• DB Only.
• Running (power and DB cut in).
• Isolated.
• DB Cutout.
To change the running status of a locomotive:
• Use the Down Arrow and Up Arrow to highlight the desired locomotive, then press the appropriate 
key to change power mode.
• When all changes are complete, press the Accept key to save changes and return to 
Train Setup.
• The Cancel key discards all changes and returns to Train Setup.
7.2.5 Change Train Data
The Change Train Data screen allows editing of railcars, loads, empties, tons, length, axles, and 
maximum train speed.
Use the Up and Down arrows to navigate between items in the train data list. Number keys are used to 
enter new values for any given train data element. When all train data edits are complete, press the 
Accept key and tons per operative brake will automatically recalculate, if necessary.
Accurate train data is critical to system performance. When changes are entered, ensure all necessary 
fields are edited, including maximum train speed. Inaccurate information can lead to poor system 
performance.
7.2.6 Verify Restrictions
Form A and B restriction information will not be displayed in non-Integrated mode. To verify restrictions, 
perform the following:
• If all restrictions are correct, press the Accept key.
• If restrictions are incorrect, press the Reject key and exit.
• Press Yes key to confirm.
• Press Start Trip key.
C P K C  |  U n i t e d  S t a t e s A i r  B r a ke  a n d  T r a i n  H a n d l i n g76

sections.title: 7 8 CPKC |  United States Air Brake and Train Handling
sections.text:
7 8 CPKC |  United States Air Brake and Train Handling
7.2.7 Trac k  S elec tion
Once Initialization is complete, the rolling map will appear and the system will prompt for current track. 
Select the appropriate track to continue. When a train is initialized on other than main track, the 
appropriate track may not be listed. Select the main track option that the train will occupy upon entering 
the main.
7.2.8  E ngaging A u to Control
The following requirements apply when engaging auto control:
• D o not comply with Trip Optimizer prompting or utilize auto control when:
o Any part of the train is on a siding or other-than-main-track location.
o Movement is within 2 miles of the end of a Track Warrant Authority.
o E x cept as provided for in Auto Through D ivergence, movement is operating on a signal less 
favorable than a proceed indication.
• When train speed is above 12 mph, the Auto Control Available message is displayed.
To engage Auto Control, perform the following:
• Press Auto Control key.
• Within 3 0  seconds, move the throttle handle to notch 8 .
• Auto Control Active message will be displayed, and the auto notch box  will appear below the 
throttle box .
7.2.9  Disengaging A u to Control
To disengage Auto Control, perform the following:
• To immediately reinstate manual control, move the throttle to match the Auto Notch position 
displayed in the Auto Throttle box ; or
• Press Manual Control key and move the throttle to match the Auto Notch position during the 3 0  
second countdown.
7.2.10  A u to Throu gh Div ergenc e
When approaching a main track divergence, approx imately 1,5 0 0  feet before the approach signal, the 
system will prompt Track Info Needed Ahead. If a diverging route is selected, Auto Active Calculating will 
appear. Once the calculations are complete, the rolling map and plan will update to accommodate the 
diverging route. The prompt will then display Auto Control Active.
If the system determines that it cannot complete the diverging route in auto, Take Manual Control Now 
will appear.
Auto control may be maintained when the train is performing a main-to-main diverging movement. Under 
these circumstances, Trip Optimizer can remain in auto control on signal indications more favorable than 
an approach.
7.3 Trip Optimizer – PTC Integrated M ode ( TO/ PTC - IM )
When equipped, PTC integrated Trip Optimizer enables the energy management system to act upon 
critical train and operating data received from PTC. 
CPKC | United States Air Brake and Train Handling 79
7.3.1 Identifying Trip Optimizer with PTC Integration
To determine if the Trip Optimizer system is integrated with PTC, perform the following:
• Initialize PTC.
• Press the Trip Optimizer key on the locomotive screen.
• Identify one of two initialization messages displayed on the welcome screen:
o Setup TO PTC Trip – PTC integrated Trip Optimizer is available.
o New Trip – PTC integrated Trip Optimizer is inactive or unavailable and will operate in stand-
alone mode.

7.3.3 Initialization

• Press the Setup TO PTC Trip key.
• Review all data displayed on the Trip Setup Screen.
• If correct, press the Accept Trip Key.
• Verify locomotive power status provided by PTC by pressing the Change Power Mode key:
o PTC will not provide the Trip Optimizer system with information related to locomotives 
operating with dynamic brake only or dynamic brakes cut out; this information must be edited 
manually.

for PTC warnings and/or enforcements.
• The system will transition to the Map screen and display Waiting for PTC on the top of the screen.

The following applies to the use of TO/PTC-IM:
• TO/PTC-IM is designated for use on PTC track only.
• Operators are prohibited from complying with Trip Optimizer prompts when any part of the train is 
located on non-PTC track.

• Movement must reach a minimum speed of 12 mph to activate auto control.
• The minimum speed to maintain auto control is 9 mph.
• TO/PTC-IM will require manual control.
o Two miles from a PTC generated stop target.
o Two miles in advance of, within, and one entire train length beyond Form B limits.
• PTC cannot recognize or enforce High Threat Urban Areas for key trains.
o Utilize manual control in High Threat Urban Areas.

approach.

CPKC | United States Air Brake and Train Handling 83
1.0 Distributed Power System Overview
Distributed power systems are designed to provide synchronous or asynchronous control of remote 
locomotive consist(s) in a train. Commands are delivered via air brake and/or radio signals.
The locomotive engineer controls each locomotive consist in the distributed power train from the lead 
locomotive. 
The term remote locomotive applies to the controlling locomotive in a remote consist. Locomotives 
connected by trainline for multiple unit service to the lead and remote locomotives are considered trail 
locomotives.
2.0 Preparing the Distributed Power System
2.1 Locomotive Conditioning and Testing Order
Condition and test distributed power locomotives in the following order:
• Condition remote locomotive(s).
• Condition the lead locomotive.
• Link to remote locomotive(s) from the lead locomotive.
• Perform a Brake Pipe Test.
• After remote locomotive(s) are placed in the train, perform a Flow Sensor Test.
• Perform a Direction Verification Test.
• Test the emergency feature if a remote is positioned at rear of train and is not equipped with a 
standalone EOT.
2.2 Conditioning Remote Locomotive(s)
Ensure that any PCS or other air brake faults are reset before attempting set up distributed power. To 
condition a remote locomotive, perform the following:
• Control Stand:
o Engine Run – Off.
o Generator Field – On.
o Control or Control/Fuel Pump – On.
o Dynamic Brake – On.
o Power Limit Switch, if equipped – Enabled.
o Reverser – Removed.
o Independent Brake – Lead and fully applied.
o Automatic Brake – Cut in and released.
• Engine Control Panel:
o Engine Control / Isolation Switch – Run.
o LEB Computer – On.
• Circuit Breakers:
o DP Radio – On.
o DP Trainline – On (Not present on all locomotives).
• Locomotive Screen:
o Select Distr Power.
o Select Remote Setup.

2.4 Linking Lead and Remote Locomotive(s)
Perform the following steps to link the lead and remote locomotive(s):
• Enter the locomotive ID and number of the remote locomotive closest to the lead locomotive.
• Press Link.
• Ensure the screen displays Link OK.
o If Link Fail is displayed, check and re-enter the number of the remote locomotive.
o If Link Fail is displayed after subsequent attempt, check the setup of the remote locomotive.
• Repeat the above steps for each additional remote locomotive consist.
o Ensure that remote locomotives are entered in accordance with their physical placement in 
the train, from front to rear.
• Press Done or Accept.
• Press DP Main Menu and check event and alarm logs for faults or other conditions.
o Air brake system failures and back-up emergency valve failures must be corrected 
before departure.
• Press Exit.
2.5 Brake Pipe Test
To perform a Brake Pipe Test, perform the following:
• Ensure the independent brake is fully applied.
• Recover PCS.
• Wait for the message Perform Brake Pipe Test.
• When flow rates have stabilized and sum of air flow is less than 90 CFM and no more than 60 
CFM at any location, Press Brk Pipe Test.
• Press Execute.
• When prompted, move the automatic brake valve handle to Minimum Reduction.
o Moving beyond the Minimum Reduction will void the test.
• If Successful, Brake Pipe Test OK will be displayed.
• If unsuccessful, repeat the above steps.
• Select DP Main Menu.
• Press Mode.
• Press Run (Or Run – FTE).
• Press Execute.
• Press Exit.

8 6 CPK C |  U nited States Air B rake and Train H andling
2.6  V al idation of  Locomotive Seq uence
Following the set up of the distributed power system, adj ustment to locomotive consist(s), or change in 
locomotive positioning, the locomotive engineer must ensure that remote locomotives are sequenced 
properly in accordance with physical placement in the train.
2.7  Fl ow Sensor Test
A Flow Sensor Test validates the Comm L oss Idle Down feature of the distributed power system. 
A Flow Sensor Test is required:
• At origin, after locomotives have been conditioned, linked, and placed in the train.
• At other than origin.
o The first-time cars are placed between a lead locomotive and remote or 
between remotes.
o Anytime 6 0  or more cars are added between a lead locomotive and remote or between 
adj acent remote consists.
To perform a Flow Sensor Test, comply with the following:
• Release the automatic brake.
• Ensure that air flow complies with AFM Test Requirements.
• Place the Distributed Power Radio circuit breaker to off.
• Make at least a 2 0 -psi reduction with the automatic brake.
• Wait for service exhaust to cease.
• Place the Distributed Power Radio circuit breaker to on.
• Ensure remote(s) display FL OW OU T, which will indicate a successful test .
• From the Remote Menu screen, normaliz e each remote by pressing Normal, then Execute.
• Move the automatic brake handle to release.
• If the test is unsuccessful, repeat the steps above.
When a lead locomotive is not equipped with breakers necessary to perform the steps listed above, 
perform a train check.
A Flow Sensor Test will fulfill the requirements of a Class III air brake test when conducted in accordance 
with required pressures. 
2.8  Directional  V erif ication Test
A directional verification test must be performed when:
• A train is first assembled with distributed power locomotive(s).
• It is suspected that the remote is not providing power in the same direction as the 
lead locomotive.
To perform a directional verification test, complete the following:
• Ensure all distributed power locomotives are in Run mode with the generator field on.
• Place all remotes in Idle, except for the remote to be tested.
• Place the reverser in forward or reverse.
• Select move to back and ensure the fence (divider line) is between L ead and Remote.
• Select Traction and Execute.
CPKC | United States Air Brake and Train Handling 87
• Release the independent brake and increase throttle effort by using the More Traction button.
• Validate that the train or train slack moves in the direction of travel indicated by the reverser.
• Repeat these steps to test each remote consist.
• When complete, select Move to Front, Normal, and Execute.
• Validate that remote(s) return to Normal and display flow rates.
2.9 Remote Locomotive in Lieu EOT
Remote locomotives may be used in lieu of a two-way EOT when a remote consist is placed at the rear of 
the train. 
To test the emergency feature of a locomotive placed at the rear of a train without an EOT, perform the 
following:
• Ensure that air flow complies with AFM Test requirements.
• To test the emergency feature with a locomotive placed at the rear of a train:
o Close a brake pipe angle cock anywhere ahead of the remote locomotive on the rear of the 
train.
 Trains with multiple remote consists must have an angle cock closed at a location 
between the last mid remote and the remote locomotive on the rear of the train.
o Place the automatic brake handle of the lead locomotive in emergency.
o Verify the emergency brake application propagates as required.
• To test the emergency feature of a light locomotive consist:
o Close the brake pipe angle cock between the remote that will be placed on the rear of the 
train and the lead consist.
o Place the automatic brake handle of the lead locomotive in emergency.
o Verify the emergency brake application propagates as required.
• Record the test results on the Crew Information Form.
3.0 Distributed Power Operating Modes and Features
3.1 System and Remote Mode Description
System and individual remote modes determine how each remote consist will respond to commands from 
the lead locomotive. 
3.2 System Operating Mode
3.2.1 Changing System Operating Mode
After completing a brake pipe test or brake pipe leakage test, change the system mode to Run to enable 
traction and dynamic brake functions of the distributed power system.
To change the operating mode, perform the following from the controlling locomotive:
• Select DP Main Menu.
• Select Mode.
• Select Run or Idle.
• Press Execute.
Run or Idle status will be displayed on the screen.

CPKC | United States Air Brake and Train Handling 87
• Release the independent brake and increase throttle effort by using the More Traction button.
• Validate that the train or train slack moves in the direction of travel indicated by the reverser.
• Repeat these steps to test each remote consist.
• When complete, select Move to Front, Normal, and Execute.
• Validate that remote(s) return to Normal and display flow rates.
2.9 Remote Locomotive in Lieu EOT
Remote locomotives may be used in lieu of a two-way EOT when a remote consist is placed at the rear of 
the train. 
To test the emergency feature of a locomotive placed at the rear of a train without an EOT, perform the 
following:
• Ensure that air flow complies with AFM Test requirements.
• To test the emergency feature with a locomotive placed at the rear of a train:
o Close a brake pipe angle cock anywhere ahead of the remote locomotive on the rear of the 
train.
 Trains with multiple remote consists must have an angle cock closed at a location 
between the last mid remote and the remote locomotive on the rear of the train.
o Place the automatic brake handle of the lead locomotive in emergency.
o Verify the emergency brake application propagates as required.
• To test the emergency feature of a light locomotive consist:
o Close the brake pipe angle cock between the remote that will be placed on the rear of the 
train and the lead consist.
o Place the automatic brake handle of the lead locomotive in emergency.
o Verify the emergency brake application propagates as required.
• Record the test results on the Crew Information Form.

3.1 System and Remote Mode Description
System and individual remote modes determine how each remote consist will respond to commands from 
the lead locomotive. 
3.2 System Operating Mode
3.2.1 Changing System Operating Mode
After completing a brake pipe test or brake pipe leakage test, change the system mode to Run to enable 
traction and dynamic brake functions of the distributed power system.
To change the operating mode, perform the following from the controlling locomotive:
• Select DP Main Menu.
• Select Mode.
• Select Run or Idle.
• Press Execute.
Run or Idle status will be displayed on the screen.

8 8 CP K C |  United States Air Brake and Train H andling
3.3 Rem ote O peratin g  M od es an d  F eatu res
3.3.1  N orm al
In normal mode, all remote traction, dynamic brake, and air brake functions are enabled. The brake valve 
may be cut in. When the distributed power system is linked and the brake pipe test is completed, the 
remote consists are in Normal.
To return a consist to Normal mode:
• Select Normal on the remote display.
o L ocomotive(s) in Stop mode should be placed into Isolate mode to be restarted before 
returning to Normal mode.
• After changing the remote to Normal, the automatic brake valve may be cut in using the following 
steps:
o Make at least a 1 0- psi reduction with the automatic brake.
o After the brake pipe exhaust has ceased, move the automatic brake handle to release.
o With the lead locomotive’s automatic brake handle in release, the remote brake 
valve will cut in when the brake pipe pressure increases at least 4 -psi at the 
remote locomotive.
3.3.2  I d l e
In Idle mode, throttle and dynamic brake functions are disabled. All remote air brake functions are 
enabled, and the brake valve may be cut in. 
To place a consist in Idle, select Idle on the remote display. This may be changed while stationary 
or moving.
3.3.3 BV  O u t
When in BV  Out mode, a locomotive will not respond to propagate air brake signals. A remote can be 
changed to BV  Out while stationary or moving.
To cut in a brake valve on a remote locomotive that has been returned to Normal or Idle:
• Make at least a 1 0- psi reduction with the automatic brake.
• After the brake pipe exhaust has ceased, move the automatic brake valve handle to release.
The brake valve will be cut in when the brake pipe pressure increases at least 4 -psi at the remote 
locomotive.
3.3.4  I sol ate
In Isolate mode, the remote’s throttle will not respond to commands and the brake valve is cut out. All air 
brake functions are disabled except emergency air brake and independent brake. A remote consist 
changes to Isolate when a communication loss idle down has occurred. 
3.3.5  Set O u t ( S/ O )
In set out mode, the remote’s throttle does not respond to commands and remains in Idle. The remote’s 
emergency brake application is enabled, and the independent brakes are fully applied. All other air brake 
functions are disabled, and the brake valve is cut out.
Set Out (S/O) mode is used to condition a remote consist left standing uncoupled from the controlling 
locomotive of a distributed power train.  
CPKC | United States Air Brake and Train Handling 89
3.3.6 Stop
In Stop mode, the remote’s throttle is set to Engine Stop. All other remote functions are set to Isolate. Use 
Stop mode to shut down locomotives when an emergency exists, such as impact, fire, hazardous material 
leak, or stop in a tunnel. The Stop mode will shut down all locomotives in the selected remote consist.
Execute Stop mode as follows:
• From the Remote display, select the remote consist to be shut down.
• Select Stop.
• Select Execute.
To return a remote to Normal after executing Stop Mode:
• Select the remote consist to be restarted.
• Select Normal.
• Select Execute.
• Manually restart each locomotive in the remote consist(s).
3.3.7 Box Car
On certain locomotive types, remote locomotives will transition to Box Car mode when the following 
conditions are met:
• Remote(s) are in a state of communication loss and an emergency or penalty brake application 
occurs.
• The penalty timer has expired.
While in box car mode, the following will apply:
• The lead locomotive will charge the brake pipe.
• When the remote brake pipe pressure rises above 60-psi, the independent brake of the remote 
consist(s) will release.
• The locomotive engineer will be able to control the train with lead consist locomotives only.
• Box car mode will be maintained until communication is restored.
When communication is restored between the lead and remote locomotive(s), a communication loss idle 
down event will be generated, and the operator screen will show Isolate mode on the affected remotes. 
The remote can be returned to Normal using the steps for Normal mode.
Box Car mode cannot be selected manually and does not apply to locomotive(s) in Set Out (S/O) mode 
prior to communication loss.  
3.3.8 BP Rise
When equipped, the distributed power system will monitor brake pipe pressure and respond as follows:
• While operating with communication between lead and remote consist(s), if an unknown brake 
pipe rise occurs while an automatic brake application is in effect, a brake pipe rise alarm will be 
displayed on the lead locomotive and the system will continue to operate in the commanded 
state.
• While operating in a state of communication loss between lead and remote consist(s), if an 
unknown brake pipe rise occurs while an automatic brake application is in effect, remote(s) will 
transition to a state of comm loss idle down and enter Isolate mode.
C P K C  |  U n i t e d  S t a t e s A i r  B r a ke  a n d  T r a i n  H a n d l i n g88

3 .3 .9  R emote S ensed Emergency  Brake Application
If equipped, remote locomotives that sense an emergency brake application will respond as follows:
• Report PC  and zero brake pipe pressure .
• Propagate the emergency application through brake pipe and radio command.
This feature does not apply to remote(s) in Set O ut (S/ O ) mode.
4.0 Modif y ing or Ending Distributed Power S et Up
4.1 Unlinking a Lead Locomotiv e f rom R emote Consist( s)  – Ending Distributed Power
When ending distributed power operation, end distributed power on the lead locomotive first.
To unlink a lead locomotive:
• Ensure the train is stopped with the independent brake fully applied and throttle in Idle.
• When distributed power is ended, the system will initiate a penalty application. Secure the 
equipment to protect against unintended movement, if required.
• From the DP Main Menu:
o Select System.
o Select U nlink .
o Select Execute.
• A penalty brake application will occur.
4.2 Unlinking R emote( s)  – Ending Distributed Power
C omplete the following steps after ending distributed power on the lead locomotive. 
To unlink remote locomotive(s):
• Fully apply the independent brake.
• O n the locomotive screen:
o Select Distr Power.
o Select End Dist Pwr.
o Press Execute.
• Ensure DP O n or DP Remote Enabled indicator is off .
• Turn off DP circuit breakers.
• Set up the control stand for either lead or trail operation.
4.3  Adding or R emov ing Locomotiv e( s)  in Lead or R emote Consist W hile Linked
If it is necessary to change out the controlling locomotive of a remote or lead consist: 
• End distributed power.
• Prepare the distributed power system as required by this section.
CPKC | United States Air Brake and Train Handling 91
4.4 Changing Ends
To change ends on a distributed power train:
• End distributed power.
• Prepare the distributed power system as required by this section.
4.5 Incremental Link and Unlink
Reserved.
5.0 Distributed Power Air Brake Tests
5.1 AFM Air Brake Test
To perform an AFM air brake test with a distributed power train:
• Press More Menu (if displayed).
• Press Remote Menu.
• Ensure each remote displays a Flow value.
• If a remote valve is out:
o Make a 10-psi reduction with the automatic brake.
o Press Normal.
o Press Execute.
o Move the automatic brake handle to release.
 Remote(s) must see a 4-psi rise in brake pipe pressure to enable a brake valve 
to cut in.
• Ensure flow does not exceed the values allowed by an AFM test and that air pressure meets the 
requirements of the air brake test being performed.
• When the signal is given to apply the brakes, make the required reduction with the automatic 
brake.
• When the signal is given to release the brakes, move the automatic brake to release.
5.2 Brake Pipe Leakage Test
A brake pipe leakage test should only be used when an AFM test cannot be performed. To conduct a 
Brake Pipe Leakage test with a distributed power train, perform the following:
• Press Remote Menu.
• Ensure remote(s) display a flow value.
• Ensure the train’s air flow and air pressure meet the requirement of the test being performed.
• Press Distr Power.
• Press DP main.
• Press System.
• Press Leakage Test.
• Press Execute.
• The distributed power system will initiate a 20-psi application of the automatic brake, allow 
pressure to stabilize, and automatically measure leakage.
• The test will take up to 3 minutes to complete and display pass or fail on the display screen.
• When prompted, place the automatic brake handle in the full service position.
• When signal is given to release the brakes, move the automatic brake handle to release.
C P K C  |  U n i t e d  S t a t e s A i r  B r a ke  a n d  T r a i n  H a n d l i n g90
